name: St Kilda Pier

facts.claim: A 300 metre elevated pier joined to a 750 metre stone breakwater in Port Phillip Bay.
The historic St Kilda Pavilion kiosk stands at the end of the pier.
A colony of about 1200 little penguins breeds among the breakwater rocks, with public viewing.

name: Rippon Lea Estate

facts.claim: A heritage-listed mansion and 14 acres of gardens in Elsternwick, cared for by the National Trust.
Built for businessman Sir Frederick Sargood, who bought the land in 1868; grounds include a lake, iron-framed fernery, ballroom and stables.
Mansion entry is by guided tour only, bought as an add-on to garden admission.

name: Werribee Park

facts.claim: An estate built on the wealth of an Australian pastoral empire, with the heritage-listed Werribee Mansion.
Formal gardens include an ornamental lake and grotto; the Victoria State Rose Garden has about 5000 roses.
Entry to the gardens and rose garden is free; the mansion costs $12.50 adult.

name: Melbourne Aquarium

facts.claim: Aquarium on the Yarra beside the Flinders Street Viaduct, with over 10,000 animals of 550+ species.
Exhibits include king and gentoo penguins, sharks, jellyfish and a saltwater crocodile.
Opened 17 January 2000 as a Southern Ocean and Antarctic aquarium.

name: Crown Entertainment Complex

facts.claim: Integrated resort of casino, hotels, restaurants and shops on the south bank of the Yarra in Southbank.
Opened at its permanent site on 8 May 1997.
Under-18s may enter the entertainment and shopping areas but not the gaming floor.

name: Ian Potter Centre

facts.claim: The home of Australian art at Federation Square, presenting Indigenous and non-Indigenous historical and contemporary art and design.
Part of the National Gallery of Victoria; entry is free, with fees only for special exhibitions.
